# manifest.yaml

<!-- GENERATED by `pnpm docs:write` from the OpenAPI document’s `ManifestYaml` schema. Do not edit: change the source and run it again. -->
Every field an app’s manifest.yaml may declare, as a table: its path, its type, whether it is required, its default, and what it means. It is documentation for the file; the platform validates with its own code, and some rules are not expressible here — see the end of this page.

| Field | Type | Required | Default | What it is |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `manifest` | `1` | yes |  | The schema version: `1`. |
| `name` | string | yes |  | The project’s slug, exactly: 3 to 39 lower-case letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter. |
| `blueprint` | string | yes |  | The project’s blueprint and its major version, `name@major` — the project’s own pin. A commit cannot change it. |
| `description` | string | no |  | What the app is for, in a sentence or two. |
| `runtime` | object | yes |  | How the app runs. |
| `runtime.port` | integer | yes |  | The port the app listens on inside its container. |
| `runtime.health` | string | no | `"/healthz"` | The path the platform checks before an instance serves: it must answer 200. A path, never a URL. |
| `runtime.command` | string or null | no | `null` | Overrides the blueprint’s entrypoint; null keeps it. |
| `runtime.build` | forbidden | no |  | FORBIDDEN: the Dockerfile is the blueprint’s. An app declares what it needs, never how to build it. |
| `resources` | object | no | `{}` | What the app may use. Unset fields take the blueprint’s defaults; the total is bounded by the project’s quota. |
| `resources.cpu` | number | no |  | CPU cores: `0.5` is half of one. |
| `resources.memory` | string | no |  | Memory, as `512Mi` or `1Gi`. |
| `resources.pids` | integer | no |  | The most processes and threads the app may run at once — a fork-bomb ceiling. |
| `resources.disk` | string | no |  | The disk the app’s volume and logs may use, as `2Gi`. |
| `services` | list of object | no | `[]` | The backing services the app needs; may be empty. |
| `services[].type` | string | yes |  | Which service: one of the platform’s catalogue, such as `mongo` or `qdrant`. |
| `services[].version` | string | yes |  | The service’s version, as a string: `"7"`. |
| `services[].name` | string | yes |  | The app’s own name for it, unique in the manifest: lower-case letters, digits and hyphens. |
| `auth` | object | no | `{}` | Who may use the app, and what it learns about them. |
| `auth.provider` | `cwl`, `none` | no | `"none"` | `cwl` signs people in with UBC’s CWL; `none` signs nobody in. |
| `auth.attributes` | list of string | no | `[]` | The CWL attributes the app receives about a signed-in person — `ubcEduCwlPuid`, `mail`, `givenName`, `sn`, `eduPersonAffiliation`. The identifier is `ubcEduCwlPuid`, never `uid`. |
| `auth.callback` | string | no | `"/auth/ubcshib/callback"` | The PATH the identity provider posts a sign-in to — Manifest derives the origin. |
| `auth.logout` | string | no | `"/auth/logout"` | The PATH single logout arrives at. |
| `ai` | object | no | `{}` | The AI the app uses, through the platform’s gateway. |
| `ai.models` | list of string | no | `[]` | The LOGICAL models the app may call — `default-chat`, `default-embed` — never a vendor’s model id. Each must be approved for `data.classification`. |
| `ai.budget` | object | no | `{}` | What the app’s AI may cost. |
| `ai.budget.project_monthly_usd` | number | no |  | The most the app may spend on AI in a month, in US dollars. Omitted, with models declared, it is the project’s AI quota; 0 is refused. |
| `ai.budget.per_user_monthly_usd` | number | no | `0` | The most one person may spend through the app in a month, in US dollars — validated and not enforced: never above the project’s AI quota, recorded with the release, and limiting no single person yet; a validation that finds it set carries a `SPEC_FIELD_NOT_ENFORCED` warning. |
| `env` | list of object | no | `[]` | Environment variables the app is given, beside the ones the platform sets. |
| `env[].name` | string | yes |  | The variable’s name: upper-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Not one the platform sets itself. |
| `env[].value` | string | no |  | Its value, written here and so in git — never a credential. |
| `env[].secret` | boolean | no |  | `true` for a value held by Manifest and never in git: set it per environment with `setAppSecret`, and a deploy is refused until it is set. |
| `egress` | object | no | `{}` | Where the app may connect to outside the platform. |
| `egress.allow` | list of string | no | `[]` | Hostnames the app may reach outside the platform — `api.ubc.ca`. Everything else is refused. |
| `data` | object | no | `{}` | What the app’s data is. |
| `data.classification` | `public`, `internal`, `confidential` | no | `"internal"` | How sensitive the app’s data is: `public`, `internal` or `confidential` — what its models must be approved for. |
| `data.retention_days` | integer | no | `365` | How many days the app keeps its data. |
| `integrations` | list of forbidden | no | `[]` | Reserved: must be empty, or absent, in schema version 1. |
| `jobs` | list of forbidden | no | `[]` | Reserved: must be empty, or absent, in schema version 1. |
| `checks` | list of forbidden | no | `[]` | Reserved: must be empty, or absent, in schema version 1. |
| `environments` | object | no | `{}` | Per-environment overrides of `resources` and `env` only. Sandbox takes the top level as written. |
| `environments.staging` | object | no |  | What changes in staging. |
| `environments.staging.resources` | object | no |  | Replaces the top-level `resources` in this environment, field by field. |
| `environments.staging.resources.cpu` | number | no |  | CPU cores: `0.5` is half of one. |
| `environments.staging.resources.memory` | string | no |  | Memory, as `512Mi` or `1Gi`. |
| `environments.staging.resources.pids` | integer | no |  | The most processes and threads the app may run at once — a fork-bomb ceiling. |
| `environments.staging.resources.disk` | string | no |  | The disk the app’s volume and logs may use, as `2Gi`. |
| `environments.staging.env` | list of object | no |  | Adds to, or replaces by name, the top-level `env` in this environment. |
| `environments.staging.env[].name` | string | yes |  | The variable’s name: upper-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Not one the platform sets itself. |
| `environments.staging.env[].value` | string | no |  | Its value, written here and so in git — never a credential. |
| `environments.staging.env[].secret` | boolean | no |  | `true` for a value held by Manifest and never in git: set it per environment with `setAppSecret`, and a deploy is refused until it is set. |
| `environments.production` | object | no |  | What changes in production. |
| `environments.production.resources` | object | no |  | Replaces the top-level `resources` in this environment, field by field. |
| `environments.production.resources.cpu` | number | no |  | CPU cores: `0.5` is half of one. |
| `environments.production.resources.memory` | string | no |  | Memory, as `512Mi` or `1Gi`. |
| `environments.production.resources.pids` | integer | no |  | The most processes and threads the app may run at once — a fork-bomb ceiling. |
| `environments.production.resources.disk` | string | no |  | The disk the app’s volume and logs may use, as `2Gi`. |
| `environments.production.env` | list of object | no |  | Adds to, or replaces by name, the top-level `env` in this environment. |
| `environments.production.env[].name` | string | yes |  | The variable’s name: upper-case letters, digits and underscores, starting with a letter. Not one the platform sets itself. |
| `environments.production.env[].value` | string | no |  | Its value, written here and so in git — never a credential. |
| `environments.production.env[].secret` | boolean | no |  | `true` for a value held by Manifest and never in git: set it per environment with `setAppSecret`, and a deploy is refused until it is set. |

## What the table cannot say

manifest.yaml, schema version 1, as a JSON Schema — DOCUMENTATION FOR THE FILE, for whoever writes it. The platform validates with its own code: `validateSpec` and a commit answer each problem as a `ManifestError` with a path, and some rules are not expressible here — the name must equal the project’s slug, a model must be in the catalogue and approved for `data.classification`, and what is asked for must fit the project’s quota.
